pr_title: [Fix #9125] Allow ConfigObsoletion to be extended by other RuboCop libraries
pr_body:
Adds the ability to add config obsoletions to extension libraries. Fixes #9125.

In order to facilitate this, I did two things, broken into separate commits.

1. I updated the obsoletions to be defined in a yaml file instead of a series of hashes. My rationale here is that it'll be simpler to configure in YAML than to try to reopen RuboCop's hashes (yes they weren't frozen but they probably should have been). In order to facilitate this, I refactored `ConfigObsoletion` and introduced `Rule` objects to encapsulate each type of rule. Each rule class is responsible for determining how it is violated, and what message to show in that case. The YAML file is parsed and converted to rules, which are then iterated over to find issues.
2. I extended the above to allow `ConfigObsoletion` to be given additional filenames to load. This will allow extensions to create their own version of `config/obsoletions.yml` (or whatever they want to call it) and tell RuboCop to load it. I also added to the documentation to explain how to use this.

Extension libraries can configure like so:

```ruby
RuboCop::ConfigObsoletion.files << filename
```

As always, feedback is welcome and I'm happy to make any changes.

pr_comments:
I like the spirit of the change overall. 

One thing I'm pondering with respect to cop renames is changing the current behavior from failing to warning and somehow accounting the for the obsolete config in RuboCop internally (e.g. merging the obsolete config and updating the cop name there or something along those lines). This will give us the flexibility to rename cops in minor releases (we clearly have many poorly named cops for historical reasons and it'd be nice if we could tackle those gradually).

As for how useful the current suggestion is for the extensions I'll defer to @koic and the @rubocop-hq/rubocop-rspec team.

Looks good!

I'm a bit concerned about the removal of `start_with?(param)`, I hope the exhaustive test coverage will prevent any regressions.
Just in case, `start_with?` was introduced [here](https://github.com/rubocop-hq/rubocop/commit/1dc32483c59ba3e61c783c09555df0615c3cc3a4#diff-b35fca184e57be3f44600ddadf6c2ceee757410050664099239e990a903d85a9R619).

> I agree that there is more that can be done here. It'd be nice if old config was automatically rewritten to the new one instead of raising an error (and having everything just be a warning like we did for #9098). I think with the rules extracted to objects it should be feasible to do this, but as a future task.

Yeah, I totally agree. I like doing changes in smaller increments in general, just wanted to share my musings based on the journey to 1.0.

> I'm a bit concerned about the removal of start_with?(param)

@pirj Yeah I added a test specifically for that rule which was previously missing. The enforced-style obsoletion type was added in #7113, and `Layout/IndentationConsistency` is the only cop using it. Looks like it previously was only the parameter `EnforcedStyle` so this shouldn't break anything as far as I see.

issue_context.title: Better support for packages: renamed / obsolete cops / config
issue_context.body:
It would be nice if packages had an API to tap into our [config_obsoletion class](https://github.com/rubocop-hq/rubocop/blob/5784d45f6c17d15c7aa72cb6d727352819351bcb/lib/rubocop/config_obsoletion.rb)

See https://github.com/rubocop-hq/rubocop-performance/issues/198#issuecomment-733497898
comments: Good idea. In general config obsoletion should be polished, so it's easier to do rename/replace stuff, without breaking the user configuration. Recently @dvandersluis did some work on that front for https://github.com/rubocop-hq/rubocop/pull/9098
I've started working on this, I hope to have something tomorrow!

review_comments: Just in case if some extension decides to override RuboCop's own cops, maybe `.reverse`? Or mix in `DEFAULT_RULE_FILE` right here, e.g. `[DEFAULT_RULE_FILE, *self.class.files].each...`?

`self.class.files` is defaulted to `[DEFAULT_RULE_FILE]` with this in mind (so that `files << ...` will append but the default will continue to be first.

I'm not sure that an extension _should_ override an obsoletion from RuboCop, but if it does, it probably should be applied?
